---
title: "Description for selectors for specific input types."
---

When specifying input types 'location', 'country', 'countryRegion', 'countryRegionCRS', 'CRS', 'crsBbox' or 'stac_assets[]', selectors are automatically created that facilitate the selection of those inputs. After being selected, those inputs appear in the `input.json` of the script or pipeline as objects with various parameters that will be available when loading then in R, Python or Julia.

For example, the 'location' selector allows the user to define a bounding box by choosing a country, region and coordinate reference system. Here is an example of an object created through the selection of the Putumayo department in Colombia, in the Bogota 1975 / Colombia West zone reference system:

``` {#location .yaml}
bbox:
  - 983337
  - 428305
  - 1360903
  - 659616
CRS:
  name: Bogota 1975 / Colombia West zone
  authority: EPSG
  code: 21896
  proj4Def: >-
    +proj=tmerc +lat_0=4.59904722222222 +lon_0=-77.0809166666667 +k=1
    +x_0=1000000 +y_0=1000000 +ellps=intl +towgs84=307,304,-318,0,0,0,0 +units=m
    +no_defs +type=crs
  unit: metre
  bbox:
    - -79.1
    - 0.03
    - -75.58
    - 10.21
country:
  englishName: Colombia
  ISO3: COL
region:
  regionName: Putumayo Department
  regionGID: COL.24_2
  countryEnglishName: Colombia
```

Here is the meaning of each key.

| Key name           | Section | Description                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| bbox               | bbox    | Array containing the minimum x, minimum y, maximum x, maximum y coordinates (in that order) of the bounding box, in units of the selected CRS. |
| name               | CRS     | Plain text name of the coordinate reference system selected.                                                                                   |
| authority          | CRS     | Authority associated with the code of the reference system. Usually EPSG or ESRI. For example `EPSG`\` for 'EPSG:4326'.                        |
| code               | CRS     | Code associated with the authority of the reference system. Usually a 4 or 5 digit integer. For example `4326`\`for EPSG:4326                  |
| proj4Def           | CRS     | Proj4 string definition of the CRS.                                                                                                            |
| wktDef             | CRS     | Well Known text definition of the CRS, when available.                                                                                         |
| unit               | CRS     | units associated with CRS. Usually `meter`, `degree`, or `feet`                                                                                |
| CRSBboxWGS84       | CRS     | The bounding box covered by this coordinate reference system, in latitude, longitude, WGS84 (EPSG:4326)                                        |
| englishName        | country | English name of the selected country, according to GADM.org.                                                                               |
| ISO3               | country | 3 letter ISO code for this | regionName         | region  | Name of the region, according to GADM                                                                                                 |
| regionGID          | region  | Identifier of the region in GADM                                                                 |
| countryEnglishName | region  | English name of the country within which this region is.                                                                                       |

When using other selectors, the object create contains a subset of the location selector. For example, the countryRegion selector will only contain the country and region sections, and countryRegionCRS will contain all but the bbox section.

## STAC assets

The `stac_assets[]` input type opens a STAC catalog browser. The user picks a catalog, a collection, then either a single item or all the tiles of the collection (on one date), and the asset to use. Several assets can be added to the selection, so the script receives a **list**, even when only one asset was chosen. A single selection has type `stac_assets`, for example to pass one asset from a script to the next.

``` {#stac_assets .yaml}
- catalog: https://stac.geobon.org
  collection: some-collection
  date: "2020-01-01"
  item: some-item
  items_are_tiles: false
  asset: data
  href: https://example.com/some-item/data.tif
  type: image/tiff; application=geotiff; profile=cloud-optimized
  categorical: false
- catalog: https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1
  collection: some-other-collection
  date: "2020-01-01"
  item: null
  items_are_tiles: true
  asset: data
  href: null
  type: image/tiff; application=geotiff; profile=cloud-optimized
  categorical: true
```

| Key name    | Description                                                                                                                                     |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| catalog     | URL of the STAC catalog.                                                                                                                        |
| collection  | Identifier of the collection in that catalog.                                                                                                   |
| date        | Day in scope, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. The day of the chosen item, or the date chosen along with `items_are_tiles`. Can be null.                              |
| item        | Identifier of the chosen item. Null when `items_are_tiles` is true.                                                                                   |
| items_are_tiles | When true, the script is expected to search the collection for all items (on `date`, if any) and mosaic their `asset` itself.                  |
| asset       | Key of the asset within the item(s).                                                                                                            |
| href        | Direct link to the asset of the chosen item. Null when `items_are_tiles` is true.                                                                     |
| type        | Media type of the asset, as declared by the catalog.                                                                                            |
| categorical | True if the asset holds classes (e.g. land cover) rather than measurements. Useful to choose a resampling method (nearest neighbour vs. bilinear). |

### Planetary Computer assets

Assets from Microsoft's Planetary Computer must be signed before they can be read. Signing works without a key, but with tight rate limits; to raise them, set `PLANETARY_COMPUTER_API_KEY` in `runner.env` and restart the server. It is then available to scripts as an environment variable.

In Python, with the `planetary-computer` and `pystac-client` packages:

``` python
import os
import planetary_computer
from pystac_client import Client

if os.environ.get("PLANETARY_COMPUTER_API_KEY"):
    planetary_computer.settings.set_subscription_key(os.environ["PLANETARY_COMPUTER_API_KEY"])

for selection in biab_inputs()["stac"]:
    if selection["items_are_tiles"]:
        catalog = Client.open(selection["catalog"], modifier=planetary_computer.sign_inplace)
        items = catalog.search(collections=[selection["collection"]], datetime=selection["date"]).items()
        hrefs = [item.assets[selection["asset"]].href for item in items]  # to be mosaicked
    else:
        hrefs = [planetary_computer.sign(selection["href"])]
```

In R, with the `rstac` package:

``` r
library(rstac)

key <- Sys.getenv("PLANETARY_COMPUTER_API_KEY")
sign_fn <- sign_planetary_computer(
  headers = if (key != "") c("Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key" = key)
)

selection <- input$stac[[1]]
found <- stac(selection$catalog) |>
  stac_search(collections = selection$collection, ids = selection$item) |>
  post_request() |>
  items_sign(sign_fn)
href <- found$features[[1]]$assets[[selection$asset]]$href
```
